adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:500 — The installer check is bypassed when the webhook has not yet created the Integration, allowing any OAuth-authenticated user with its installation ID to attach the victim installation through the earlier next_step branch.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the GitHubInstallation.dispatch method, when Integration.DoesNotExist is caught (line 488-489), the code calls `return pipeline.next_step()` without performing the installer verification check that happens later (lines 500-505). This means if the webhook hasn't created the Integration yet, any OAuth-authenticated user who knows the installation_id can proceed through the pipeline without the sender login verification. The check at lines 500-505 only runs when the Integration exists but OrganizationIntegration doesn't, creating a race condition where an attacker could claim an installation before the legitimate webhook creates the Integration record.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:482 — A callback arriving before the installation webhook creates its Integration skips installer verification and links the unverified installation.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, when Integration.DoesNotExist is caught at line 482, the code simply calls `return pipeline.next_step()` without any verification of the authenticated user. The verification logic (comparing github_authenticated_user to integration.metadata['sender']['login']) only happens in the else branch when the Integration already exists. This means if the OAuth callback arrives before the GitHub webhook creates the Integration record, the installation proceeds without verifying that the authenticated user matches the installer, bypassing the security check that was intended to be added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:423 — Token exchange transport failures escape the try block and turn transient GitHub outages into an unhandled installation failure instead of the failure dialog.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at lines 418-427 in the diff, the try block only wraps `safe_urlread(req).decode('utf-8')` and `dict(parse_qsl(body))`. However, `safe_urlopen()` on line 418 is called BEFORE the try block, so any network/transport failures from that call (timeouts, connection errors, etc.) would raise an unhandled exception rather than being caught and returning the error dialog. This is a real bug where transient GitHub outages during token exchange would cause an unhandled exception instead of the graceful error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:481 — A missing Integration skips ownership verification, allowing an authenticated attacker to claim another installation ID before its webhook creates the row.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, when Integration.DoesNotExist is caught at line 481, the code simply calls `return pipeline.next_step()` without any ownership verification. The new security check that compares `github_authenticated_user` with `integration.metadata['sender']['login']` only runs when the Integration already exists (lines 489-496). This means if an attacker authenticates via OAuth and provides an installation_id before the legitimate webhook creates the Integration row, they can proceed through the pipeline without the sender verification check. This is a race condition security vulnerability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:392 — The installation-not-found test supplies an unrelated OAuth state and asserts the generic auth error, so it can pass without exercising the mocked GitHub 404 or detecting broken missing-installation handling.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the test_installation_not_found test at line 385-401 uses a state value 'ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05' that doesn't match the pipeline signature '9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3' used in other tests. Looking at the OAuthLoginView code (lines 410-413), when the state doesn't match pipeline.signature, it returns an error immediately without proceeding to check the installation. This means the test passes by hitting the OAuth state validation error rather than actually testing the 'installation not found' scenario. The test name and intent don't match what's actually being tested.
